subtitle: Washington reads Tokyo's answer
photoCredit: Secretary of State Cordell Hull with Japan's envoys Kichisaburo Nomura and Saburo Kurusu, 17 November 1941. Public domain.
body:
At about 9:30 tonight, a Navy officer hands the President a locked pouch. Inside are thirteen decoded parts of Japan's fourteen part reply to the American terms.

Franklin Roosevelt reads for about ten minutes and passes the pages to Harry Hopkins. Then he says, in substance: "This means war."

Half an hour earlier, his personal appeal to Emperor Hirohito went out by cable, asking him to give thought to "ways of dispelling the dark clouds." The fourteenth part has not arrived.
